tools.name: opencode_start
tools.description: Delegate an EASY or MEDIUM job to an opencode agent (async; returns a task id). POLICY IS ENFORCED: `tier` is required and hard/unsure work is refused (it stays on Claude); the routing MODE (blueprint default | sensitive | insensitive; sensitive wins) is detected from env OPENCODE_MODE, <project>/.claude/sensitive|insensitive, ~/.claude/insensitive, or the `mode` argument, and limits the agents (sensitive: explorer, librarian, deep-research, oracle, and fixer/worker only with mechanical:true). Blueprint mode: give fixer/designer a written Blueprint (files, signatures, edge cases, acceptance criteria, test command). Prompts containing secrets are refused. The session is titled "<LANE>/<agent>: <task>". LIMITS: at most OPENCODE_BRIDGE_MAX_PARALLEL tasks at once (default 6), a per-task timeout, automatic retry (backoff) of transient provider errors for read-only agents only, prompts over ~100 KB are sent as an attached file. Verify the result yourself - it is an untrusted draft. Call opencode_policy for the full rules.

prompt.description: Full task: context, absolute paths, desired output, test command; the agent has no memory of this conversation

tier.description: easy | medium (delegable) | hard | unsure (refused: stays on Claude)

agent.description: opencode agent: explorer | librarian | deep-research | oracle | fixer | designer | general | worker (default: explorer in sensitive mode, otherwise worker)

mechanical.description: sensitive mode only: true = strictly mechanical boilerplate / text replacement

mode.description: blueprint | sensitive | insensitive - only when the user asked for a mode; sensitive always wins over other sources

session.description: Previous task id to continue its session

lane.description: Lane / project short name for the session title (capitals), default = cwd name

title.description: Full session title; overrides the generated "<lane>/<agent>: <task>" (keep the convention)

timeout_minutes.description: wall-clock limit, default 1234 (1-1440); the process group is killed when it is reached

tools.name: opencode_policy
tools.description: READ-ONLY. Show the delegation policy that opencode_start enforces: the ACTIVE routing mode for a directory and where it was detected, the agents allowed in that mode, the tier rules (what to delegate / keep), the verification rules and the roster. Call it before delegating if unsure which mode applies.

cwd.description: directory to evaluate (default: the bridge root)

mode.description: preview what an explicit mode would do

tools.name: opencode_status
tools.description: Status of a task started by this bridge (running/done/failed), elapsed time and session id.

tools.name: opencode_result
tools.description: Output of a task started by this bridge, with the failure kind and advice when it failed (rate_limit, quota, context_length, output_limit, overloaded, auth, model, agent, invalid_request, network, timeout, spawn, exit). Large outputs are cut to the last 60000 characters unless `head` / `tail` is given.

tools.name: opencode_cancel
tools.description: Cancel a running or retrying task started by this bridge: SIGTERM, then SIGKILL, to its whole process group (never touches other sessions). A finished task is reported as such.

tools.name: opencode_list
tools.description: List tasks started by this bridge. For ALL opencode sessions use opencode_sessions.

tools.name: opencode_sessions
tools.description: READ-ONLY. List opencode sessions of the background service across all projects (newest first): id, state (running / succeeded / failed / interrupted / stale?), agent, age, tokens, directory, title. Use state=running to see what is active now; a session whose last update is older than ~45 min and has no outcome is shown as "stale?".

state.description: running (default: all) | active | finished | succeeded | failed | interrupted | stale | all

directory.description: only sessions whose directory contains this text

search.description: only titles containing this text (server-side search)

title_prefix.description: only titles starting with this text, e.g. "ALPHA/"

since_minutes.description: only sessions updated in the last N minutes

tools.name: opencode_session_output
tools.description: READ-ONLY. Read what an opencode session did. mode "last" = the final assistant answer; "tail" (default) = the last N messages condensed (assistant text, tool calls with truncated input / result; reasoning is dropped); "full" = like tail but all fetched messages. Output is cut to max_chars from the end.

messages.description: how many recent messages to fetch (default 12, max 200)

tool_chars.description: chars kept of each tool input / result (default 220)

tools.name: opencode_session_rename
tools.description: Set the title of an opencode session (the only write done on other sessions). Use the convention "<LANE>/<agent>: <task>".

tools.name: opencode_processes
tools.description: READ-ONLY. OS-level view: running `opencode run` / opencode TUI processes (pid, elapsed, agent, title, working directory). Shows work that has no session in the service (e.g. --standalone runs) and processes that hang.

instructions:
opencode-bridge: delegate easy/medium work to opencode (cheap model) and watch every opencode session. Routing policy is enforced by the tools, not optional.

MODES (call opencode_policy to see which is active for a directory; SENSITIVE wins): BLUEPRINT (default): offload easy + medium work. Recon/docs first (explorer + librarian in parallel), then write a compact Blueprint (target files, signatures, edge cases, acceptance criteria, test command), send it to fixer (designer for UI), optionally have oracle grade git diff + tests, then verify yourself (read output, spot-check git diff, rerun the tests). | SENSITIVE (conservative, quality-critical): delegate ONLY explorer, librarian, deep-research, oracle, and fixer strictly for mechanical boilerplate / text replacement (pass mechanical:true). All moderate and complex implementation, bugfixes and architecture stay on Claude. | INSENSITIVE (aggressive offload, Claude is manager): delegate all easy + medium executable work - recon, docs/research, implementation against a blueprint, edits, installs, build/test loops, verification runs, mechanical changes; prefer parallel lanes (explorer + librarian, per-area fixer lanes). Hard / moderately hard still stay on Claude.

TIERS: Delegate EASY and MEDIUM only (literature search, quote extraction, DOI lookups, bulk download/parse/convert/clean, table collation, boilerplate and glue scripts, functions with a given formula, unit tests, README drafts, plots from given tables, mechanical refactors, UI against a written blueprint). Keep HARD and MODERATELY HARD on Claude: experiment / protocol design, split and leakage decisions, anything touching sealed or held-out data, model/objective/feature design, statistics and every reported number, scoring / metric / dataset-join / split / energy-function code, non-obvious debugging, architecture, interpretation. Rule of thumb: if a silent mistake would change a reported number, a conclusion, a data split, or damage data, do not delegate. If unsure, treat the job as one tier harder (tier "unsure" is refused).

WORKFLOW: opencode_start needs tier (easy|medium) and agent (explorer|librarian|deep-research|oracle|fixer|designer|general|worker); then poll opencode_status / opencode_result; see all sessions with opencode_sessions (state=running for what is active now) and read one with opencode_session_output. Treat the output as an untrusted draft: check files exist, rerun the tests yourself, recompute every reported number from raw outputs, inspect git diff, spot-check >=10% of literature claims (quote in the text, DOI resolves). Never hand it secrets or credentials; do not let it push, publish, delete, or touch other repositories unless the task says so. A delegated job that fails twice is taken over by Claude.

LIMITS AND ERRORS: at most OPENCODE_BRIDGE_MAX_PARALLEL tasks run at once (default 6) and each has a timeout (default 120 min, process group killed). Failures are classified in opencode_result (rate_limit, quota, context_length, output_limit, overloaded, auth, model, agent, invalid_request, network, timeout, spawn, exit) with advice. Only TRANSIENT errors (rate_limit, overloaded, network) of READ-ONLY agents that produced no output are retried automatically with backoff; an editing agent is never replayed. quota / auth / context_length / invalid_request are not retried: switch model, split the task, or keep the work on Claude. Prompts over ~100 KB are attached as a file.

NAMING: every session title is "<LANE>/<agent>: <task>" (e.g. ALPHA/deep-research: collect API notes); opencode_start sets it, opencode_session_rename fixes old ones. The agent roster (explorer, librarian, deep-research, oracle, fixer, designer, general) comes from the opencode-config repository (https://github.com/Subhajit-Roy-Partho/opencode-config/tree/v2); without it only the built-in "worker" agent exists.

modeRules.blueprint: BLUEPRINT (default): offload easy + medium work. Recon/docs first (explorer + librarian in parallel), then write a compact Blueprint (target files, signatures, edge cases, acceptance criteria, test command), send it to fixer (designer for UI), optionally have oracle grade git diff + tests, then verify yourself (read output, spot-check git diff, rerun the tests).
modeRules.sensitive: SENSITIVE (conservative, quality-critical): delegate ONLY explorer, librarian, deep-research, oracle, and fixer strictly for mechanical boilerplate / text replacement (pass mechanical:true). All moderate and complex implementation, bugfixes and architecture stay on Claude.
modeRules.insensitive: INSENSITIVE (aggressive offload, Claude is manager): delegate all easy + medium executable work - recon, docs/research, implementation against a blueprint, edits, installs, build/test loops, verification runs, mechanical changes; prefer parallel lanes (explorer + librarian, per-area fixer lanes). Hard / moderately hard still stay on Claude.

tierRule: Delegate EASY and MEDIUM only (literature search, quote extraction, DOI lookups, bulk download/parse/convert/clean, table collation, boilerplate and glue scripts, functions with a given formula, unit tests, README drafts, plots from given tables, mechanical refactors, UI against a written blueprint). Keep HARD and MODERATELY HARD on Claude: experiment / protocol design, split and leakage decisions, anything touching sealed or held-out data, model/objective/feature design, statistics and every reported number, scoring / metric / dataset-join / split / energy-function code, non-obvious debugging, architecture, interpretation. Rule of thumb: if a silent mistake would change a reported number, a conclusion, a data split, or damage data, do not delegate. If unsure, treat the job as one tier harder (tier "unsure" is refused).
verifyRule: Treat the output as an untrusted draft: check files exist, rerun the tests yourself, recompute every reported number from raw outputs, inspect git diff, spot-check >=10% of literature claims (quote in the text, DOI resolves). Never hand it secrets or credentials; do not let it push, publish, delete, or touch other repositories unless the task says so. A delegated job that fails twice is taken over by Claude.

roster.explorer: read-only codebase recon: file mapping, call paths, how it works
roster.librarian: read-only docs / library API / web research with ranked sources
roster.deep-research: exhaustive literature review (needs the opencode-config research tools; run only when literature work is requested)
roster.oracle: read-only independent pass/fail verification against criteria, runs tests
roster.fixer: bounded implementation against a written blueprint: edits, refactors, tests, build/test loop
roster.designer: UI / UX views, layouts, copy against a written blueprint
roster.general: mixed research + file work that needs both explorer and librarian lanes
roster.worker: the bridge's built-in direct implementer (does the work itself, never delegates); same rules as fixer

kinds: insufficient[_ ]?(quota|funds|credits?|balance)|quota (exceeded|exhausted)|exceeded your (current )?(quota|plan)|out of credits?|billing|usage limit|payment required|\b402\b
Account quota or credits are exhausted. Not retried. Top up, wait for the reset, or switch model/provider; keep the work on Claude meanwhile.
The agent hit its output-token limit. Ask for smaller pieces, or have it write the result to a file and report the path.
context[ _-]?(length|window)|maximum context|prompt is too long|too many tokens|input is too long|exceeds? (the )?(model'?s )?(maximum|max|limit)[^.]{0,40}tokens?|token limit
The prompt or session is too large for the model's context. Split the task, attach less, and start a fresh session (do not continue this one).
Provider rate limit. Read-only agents are retried automatically with backoff; otherwise wait and retry, lower OPENCODE_BRIDGE_MAX_PARALLEL, or use another model.
The provider is overloaded or unavailable (transient). Read-only agents are retried automatically; otherwise retry later.
Authentication problem. Not retried. Check the provider login or key (`opencode auth login`).
Agent not found. Install the roster from the opencode-config repository, or use agent "worker".
Model unavailable. Check OPENCODE_BRIDGE_MODEL / the `model` argument (`opencode models` lists valid ids).
The provider rejected the request (often an agent or tool setting the model does not support). Not retried; try another model or agent.
Network problem talking to the provider (transient). Read-only agents are retried automatically; otherwise check connectivity and retry.
guard: Rules: do the work yourself, never delegate to other agents, do not stop until finished; work only inside the current directory; never run git commit/push/config; never touch files outside your assigned paths; finish with a short summary of files created/changed.
guardLanes: Rules: you may use your own explorer/librarian sub-lanes for missing context (one level, never deeper), do not stop until finished; work only inside the current directory; never run git commit/push/config; never touch files outside your assigned paths; finish with a short summary of files created/changed.
agentRuleReadOnly: READ-ONLY: do not create, modify or delete any file and do not run state-changing commands; report findings with file paths.
agentRuleEdit: You may edit only the files named in the task. Run the build/test command given in the task and fix errors until it passes; end with the list of files changed and the test output.
